summary:
Submitted a research product that folds the third confirmed result and one reading-derived protection back into the implementation map.

Context from the index: all three findings are now confirmed_in_scope (oblig-config-from-durable-entry, oblig-config-readout-index, oblig-config-committed-backed-by-entry), pending_work is empty, map v5 is the accepted basis, and capacity still holds 1 audit unit, 3 semantic reviews and 5 experiments.

Product contents (draft-relative submission.json with the updated map.json):

Map handoff, two clarifications with source citations. b-config-change replaces its answered question with the sourced conditional relationship: a node holding an adopted configuration keeps campaigning under it because latestIndex differs from committedIndex, a fresh peer with an empty configuration can supply the missing vote, and the leader commit path promotes the adopted configuration to committed without consulting the entry stored at its index; only the restart-survival question remains. b-fsm-apply replaces its unanswered rollback question with the protection that the FSM receives only entries admitted up to the commit index and a committed entry is not truncated under the election restriction, so the rollback that exists applies to the uncommitted latest configuration; its residual states that this chain is a reading argument rather than an execution result.

The accompanying feedback (ref_ids b-config-change, b-fsm-apply) records both answered propositions, keeps the reading-derived part honestly flagged, and carries forward the remaining frontier: restart survival of an unsupported committed configuration, the heartbeat term-regression pair and the election-restriction chain, the pre-vote and TimeoutNow premises, the external consumers of the configuration index, and the majority-intersection residual.

Preflight `validate` returned valid=true with no diagnostics. Acceptance and version assignment remain with the controller.
